narrative: New England fell to JAX 6-35. The offense posted -0.25 EPA/play (37% success rate) while the defense allowed 0.23 EPA/play. Turnover margin was -2.

good: Rhamondre Stevenson was our silver lining, adding 7% win probability on a day when almost everything went wrong.
Marcus Jones notched his first interception of the season, giving the defense at least one bright moment in Jacksonville.
bad: Drake Maye threw two interceptions and lost a fumble — three turnovers that completely derailed any offensive rhythm we might have built.
Red zone catastrophe: we scored zero touchdowns on four trips while Jacksonville punched in five scores on five attempts, a devastating 0-for-4 versus 5-for-5 split.
Our defense allowed Jacksonville to convert eight of twelve third downs (67%), well above the league norm of 40%.
ugly: An offensive performance that generated minus-0.25 EPA per play, meaningfully below the league average of zero, and a defensive showing that allowed plus-0.23 EPA per play — the kind of two-sided collapse that makes 35-6 feel inevitable rather than surprising.

playerOfTheGame.reason: Led the team with +7% win probability added.

fanTake: Look, there's no way around it: Jacksonville came to play and we came to get embarrassed. A 35-6 loss on the road where our defense allowed five touchdowns on five red-zone trips, our offense managed zero touchdowns despite four trips into the end zone, and Drake Maye turned the ball over three times — that's not a competitive football game, that's a disaster. The stats tell the whole grim story: we were minus-0.25 EPA per play on offense, our defense yielded plus-0.23, and we lost the turnover battle by two. When your quarterback calls his own performance "unacceptable" and the entire offensive unit deserves the same verdict, you know this one stings.
